title: Nonnegative signed insertion equations with singleton degree-zero projection
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $r\in\mathbb N$, $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X.\mathrm{Opens}$, $G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $i:\operatorname{Fin}(r)$. Let $A$ and $C$ be the restrictions to $U_i$ of the integer extensions of $G[0]$ and the alternating complex of [def-pc-s3-alternating-cech-sheaf-construction], and let $a:A\to C$ be its restricted augmentation. There exist a morphism $\pi:C^0\to A^0$ and module-sheaf morphisms $h_k:C^{k+1}\to C^k$ such that $d_0h_0+\pi a^0=1_{C^0}$ and $d_kh_k+h_{k-1}d_{k-1}=1_{C^k}$ for every integer $k>0$. Composites use Lean order, and the second term uses $C^k\cong C^{k-1+1}$. No equation for $k<0$, no chain retraction, and no adjustment to any other projection are required.

source.place: Tag 02FU, local insertion and cancellation; increasing-tuple adaptation of the alternating convention of Tag 01FM

proof.text: Choose positive-degree insertion maps h from [lem-pc-s3-alternating-cech-sheaf-positive-contraction]. At degree one the equation is d_1 h_1+h_0 d_0=id. Precompose by d_0 and use d_0 d_1=0 to see that f=id-d_0 h_0 is killed by d_0.
Apply [lem-pc-s3-alternating-cech-sheaf-degree-zero-factorization] to f, obtaining π with π a_0=f. Then d_0 h_0+π a_0=d_0 h_0+(id-d_0 h_0)=id. The positive-degree equations are those of h.

theorem alternatingCechSheafAugmentation_restrict_singleton_contraction
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {r : ℕ} (U : Fin r → X.Opens) (G : X.Modules) (i : Fin r) :
    let F := Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U i).ι
    let A := (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
      (((CochainComplex.single₀ X.Modules).obj G).extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)
    let C := (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
      ((alternatingCechSheafComplex U G).extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)
    let a : A ⟶ C := (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map
      (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (alternatingCechSheafAugmentation U G)
        ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)
    ∃ π : C.X 0 ⟶ A.X 0,
      ∃ h : ∀ k : ℤ, C.X (k + 1) ⟶ C.X k,
        (C.d (0 : ℤ) (0 + 1) ≫ h 0 + π ≫ a.f 0 = 𝟙 (C.X 0)) ∧
        ∀ k : ℤ, 0 < k → C.d k (k + 1) ≫ h k +
          (C.XIsoOfEq (show k = k - 1 + 1 by omega)).hom ≫
            h (k - 1) ≫ C.d (k - 1) k = 𝟙 (C.X k)
